result:
The 6-second composition is in `./promo/`, and `npx hyperframes check` passes with 0 errors and 0 warnings. That covers lint, runtime, layout, motion, contrast (20/20 text checks) and craft. I haven't previewed or rendered it. The skill says to wait for your approval before rendering.

- **`index.html`:** the root is 1920×1080 at 30 fps for 6 s, with a cream background layer, the voiceover audio, and one captions host on its own caption track.
- **`compositions/captions.html`:** the captions are a single group, "SHIP FASTER WITH GIRTH", at 120px and centred inside the title-safe area. Each word goes faint, then coral-highlighted while it's spoken, then solid. State changes use seek-safe `tl.set` calls.
- **Word timings:** the skill says not to invent them, so I generated a voiceover with `hyperframes tts` and ran `hyperframes transcribe` on it. The timings are Ship 0–0.256 s, faster 0.256–0.64 s, with 0.64–0.896 s and Girth 0.896–1.28 s. The voice runs 1.3 s, so the highlight finishes early and the finished headline stays on screen until 6 s. Transcription returned the last word lowercase, so I capitalised "Girth" in the display text.
- **Fixes after the first check:** it raised three warnings. I added an id to the background layer and `data-no-timeline` to the root, and I moved the voice and captions to start at 0 s so frame 0 isn't empty.

I added the voiceover audio, which you didn't ask for, because it was the only way to get real word timings. Delete the `<audio>` line in `index.html` if you want it silent. The captions would then have no timing source.

The next step is `npx hyperframes preview --background` so you can review it, then a render once you approve.
